persistence_invariants.brief: A UNIQUE constraint on (sku, location) rejects a second row for the same pair at the DB level; the upsert path relies on it as its ON CONFLICT target.
sku is NOT NULL: inserting a row with a null sku is rejected by the database.
location is NOT NULL: inserting a row with a null location is rejected by the database.
quantity is NOT NULL: inserting a row with a null quantity is rejected by the database (tracking_code is deliberately nullable — absent renders as 'not tracked').
A CHECK (quantity >= 0) constraint rejects a negative quantity at write time; no negative stock is ever stored.
Filing an existing (sku, location) is a single atomic INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE: after the write exactly one row exists for the pair carrying the new quantity and tracking_code.

The initial create_table migration is reversible: after downgrade to its own down_revision and upgrade head, stock_records and its columns, UNIQUE(sku, location) and CHECK(quantity >= 0) constraints are present again (schema recreated; no row-survival claim for the initial create).

S2-stock-by-location-table adds an ADDITIVE revision on the pre-existing stock_records (down_revision = the S1 create revision) creating btree ix_stock_records_location_sku (location, sku) for AP2. Downgrading to its down_revision drops only that index while stock_records and its existing rows persist unchanged; upgrade head recreates the index.

access_patterns.brief: SELECT DISTINCT location ORDER BY location to populate the field-location / retrieve-location combobox options.

SELECT sku, location, quantity, tracking_code FROM stock_records WHERE quantity > 0 [AND location = :loc] ORDER BY location, sku for the home stock-by-location table and its warehouse-select filter (quantity-0 rows hidden per OD3; UNIQUE(sku, location) leads on sku, so it does not serve a location-only filter). Realized by the S2 additive migration adding ix_stock_records_location_sku (location, sku) (PI8, db-design SC5).

api_contracts.item: Request {sku: str, location: str, quantity: int>=0, tracking_code: str|null}. Response 200 {sku: str, location: str, quantity: int, tracking_code: str|null, created: bool} (created=false when an existing (sku, location) was updated in place). 422 {errors: [{field: str, message: str}]} naming the offending field.
200 {sku: str, location: str, quantity: int, tracking_code: str|null}; 404 {detail: str} when no record exists for the pair (renders retrieve-empty).

Bare JSON array of distinct location strings (non-null) over ALL stock_records rows INCLUDING quantity-0 rows (so a location on record with no stock is still offered), sorted ascending; empty array when no stock is on record.

Bare JSON array of {sku: str, location: str, quantity: int>0, tracking_code: str|null}, one per STOCKED (sku, location) record: rows with quantity = 0 are EXCLUDED (WHERE quantity > 0), ordered by location then sku; optional location filter; empty array when no stocked record matches, including a location whose only rows are at quantity 0 (renders stock-empty).

200 {sku: str, par_level: int|null (always null in F1 - no par level stored), locations: [{location: str, quantity: int>0, tracking_code: str|null}]} with locations ordered by location, only this SKU's STOCKED rows (quantity-0 rows excluded per OD3); locations is [] for a SKU with no stocked row (never filed or only quantity-0 rows) - still 200, never 404 (OD1: stock_records is the SKU authority).

nfrs.requirement: Stock data survives every schema migration. F1 has two migrations: the initial create_table (S1), whose guarantee is schema reversibility (PI7), and the S2 additive index migration ix_stock_records_location_sku (location, sku) on the pre-existing stock_records, whose guarantee is that rows filed before it persist across its downgrade/upgrade (PI8). The adjustment timestamp/actor clause is N/A for F1 (read-and-record only; no adjustment operation — owned by the adjustment feature).

fitness_functions.clause: Downgrade the stock_records create migration to its down_revision then upgrade head on the paired branch; the table with its UNIQUE(sku, location) and CHECK(quantity >= 0) constraints is present again.

With stock rows filed, downgrade the S2 add-index migration (ix_stock_records_location_sku) to its down_revision then upgrade head on the paired branch; every previously filed row persists unchanged and the index exists again.

nfrs.fitness_function: Real-branch migration tests per fitness_functions clause: S1 create_table downgrade/upgrade recreates the schema (PI7); S2 add-index downgrade/upgrade preserves filed rows and recreates ix_stock_records_location_sku (PI8).
Filing stock with a negative quantity is rejected (422 naming 'quantity') and no row is stored on the paired branch; a direct insert of quantity < 0 is rejected by the CHECK constraint.
nfrs.requirement: Stock never goes below zero: a negative quantity is rejected at write time (boundary validation naming the quantity field + DB CHECK PI5). The no-overcommit clause is N/A for F1: no pick/allocation operation exists in this feature (owned by the pick feature).

fitness_functions.clause: Filing the same (sku, location) twice leaves exactly one stock_records row for the pair, carrying the second write's values.
A re-file of an existing (sku, location) returns 200 with created=false (a normal confirmation), never a 4xx/5xx.
A stock record is addressable by (sku, location): GET /api/stock?sku=&location= returns exactly that pair's record.

nfrs.requirement: Every (sku, location) is uniquely addressable; a collision is resolved at write time by update-in-place, never a duplicate and never an error page.
nfrs.fitness_function: Real-branch tests per fitness_functions clause: double-file leaves one row; re-file returns 200 created=false; GET by (sku, location) returns that pair.
The integration test session asserts DATABASE_URL is a postgresql URL to the paired branch (not sqlite/in-memory) before any test runs, failing the suite otherwise.
nfrs.requirement: Integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch (databricks_postgres via DATABASE_URL), never a mock or in-memory DB.

nfrs.fitness_function: Every /api/* endpoint declared in api_contracts responds with Content-Type application/json (no text/html).
nfrs.requirement: The UI is a React + TypeScript SPA under client/; the boundary returns JSON only, never server-rendered HTML.
Inward dependencies boundary -> service -> repository -> models; only repositories touch the ORM session (get_session in app/repositories/session.py, re-exported by the service).
nfrs.fitness_function: N/A – defended deterministically by the consort-layering-clean gate; no per-story fitness test.

nfrs.requirement: DB connection comes only from the substrate-written DATABASE_URL (databricks_postgres); no hard-coded credentials or DB name.

open_decisions.question: Is stock_records the authority on whether a SKU is 'known' (first filing establishes the SKU), or will a later feature introduce a separate SKU catalog?
When the combined tracking_code is split into location/batch/serial (F6), is it an additive column migration on stock_records preserving existing codes?

Locations are derived from stock_records (no locations table), so how is a location 'on record but with no stock' represented: rows at quantity 0 (and does the filtered table then hide zero-quantity rows), or a separate locations registry?
open_decisions.resolution: A location 'on record with no stock' is one whose stock_records rows are all at quantity 0 (no locations registry). EP4 GET /api/stock/records excludes quantity-0 rows, so filtering to such a location returns [] and renders stock-empty; EP3 GET /api/locations still lists it (distinct over all rows), so warehouse-select offers it. Consistent with S1: a quantity-0 filing is valid (CHECK quantity >= 0) and S1 AC2 retrieve by (sku, location) via EP2 still returns the qty-0 record.

open_decisions.question: Where will a SKU's par level be stored (a per-SKU or per-(sku, location) column/table) when a later feature tracks it? F1 stores none and EP5 returns par_level null.
